# Upātidhāvanti Sutta (Ud 6.9 (PTS Ud 72))

**ID:** Ud 6.9 (PTS Ud 72)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upātidhāvanti Sutta* is the ninth discourse of the sixth chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, cataloged at page 72 of the Pali Text Society edition [SuttaCentral]. The discourse delivers an inspired utterance centered on the imagery of insects flying into the open flames of lamps set out during the night [SuttaCentral].

Passage-level parallels to the verse are identified across multiple recensions of the *Udānavarga* tradition, specifically corresponding to chapter 29 (the *Yugavarga* or "Day and Night" chapter; Chinese 相應品 / 雙要品) in Sanskrit texts (UV 29, UVS 29), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 29), and Chinese translations in the Taishō canon (T 212.30 and T 213.29) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, computational analysis by DharmaNexus records internal Pali text-reuse alignments in the introductory narrative frame (§0.2–1.3), which is shared with other discourses in the *Udāna*, including the *Nanda Sutta* (Ud 3.2), the *Sundarī Sutta* (Ud 4.8), and the *Catutthanibbānapaṭisaṁyutta Sutta* (Ud 8.4) [DharmaNexus].

The sutta is represented on SuttaCentral with sixteen translations across thirteen modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
